issues.issue: The right-side patch-in-place machinery is clipped by the frame edge, creating a slightly awkward close-up composition.
issues.fix: Pull the camera back or pan slightly left/right so the cropped gantry/road edge is either fully visible or cleanly out of frame.

issues.issue: A server and blue patch-group base are cut off at the lower-right edge, which looks accidental in the close framing.
issues.fix: Reframe slightly left/up or remove the partial server from the edge of the shot.

issues.issue: A server and blue patch-group base are still partially clipped at the lower-right edge.
issues.fix: Adjust the camera or crop so the partial server is either fully included or not visible.

issues.issue: The report is titled “Patch result · every server,” but the visible rows are groups (“Database group,” “Code-hosting group”) rather than individual servers. This breaks the rule that reports list each server’s patch result.
issues.fix: Change the rows to generic per-server entries, such as “Database server,” “Code-hosting server,” and “Backup host,” without using real host names or IDs.

issues.issue: The “No patch data” row and its flag text are extremely low-contrast and hard to read at 720p.
issues.fix: Do not show that row until it can appear at readable contrast, or increase its opacity/contrast in this frame.

issues.issue: The report is still labeled “every server” but lists group-level rows, not per-server patch results.
issues.fix: Use generic per-server rows instead of group rows while keeping the output public-safe.

issues.issue: The row says “flagged in the daily report,” but the requirement says daily and weekly reports flag servers with no patch data. This wording implies only the daily report.
issues.fix: Change the badge to “flagged in daily + weekly reports” or simply “flagged in reports.”

review.overall: Most frames are readable and consistent with the required patching flow. The main compliance problem is in the final report cards: they must show per-server patch results, not group-level results, and the no-patch-data flag should reflect both daily and weekly reporting.
